scope.purpose: Describe an object with a short, read-only status or category word (Draft, Paid, Overdue, Beta) set by the application, in a small colored box whose words carry the meaning and whose color reinforces it.
useCases: A status in a table cell, a list item, a card or a page header (Active, Pending, Failed).
A category without valence (Internal, Archived) with the neutral intent, or a highlighted one in the brand color (New, Beta) with the accent intent.
A stronger signal with the strong appearance (a critical status that must stand out in a dense list).
An optional leading icon that repeats the status shape (check, warning) for faster scanning.
exclusions: Values the user manipulates (removable keywords, active filters, MultiSelect values, user labels), with or without a count: Tag (later candidate).
A dot without text: a later indicator.
Badges positioned over another element (avatar or icon corner): a later composition.
Badges inside a Button slot: a quantity in a Button is a Counter.
Live announcements when a status changes: the integration owns live regions.
alternatives: Tag (later) for a value the user can remove or select.
Plain text when the status is part of a sentence.
Alert (wave 3) for a message that explains the status.

contract.scope: Badge contract: required label, intent (neutral, accent, info, success, warning, danger; default neutral), appearance (subtle, strong), size (sm, md, lg); container, leading (at most one Icon) and label parts; no state; color.status.{intent}.* roles, border.width.default, radius.indicator, typography.indicator.{size}, space.content.xs paddings and gap, size.icon.xs; nine rules (read-only text carrying the meaning, appearances, one-line truncation, Counter box family, optical icon placement, no interaction, forced colors). The neutral and accent status roles are recorded in the semantic approval.

decisionsTaken: Colors from the approved color.status.{intent}.* family (surface, content, border, icon for subtle; surfaceStrong and contentStrong for strong) instead of a new indicator family: Badge is the status display the family was named for; the counter's colored emphasis stays deferred.

Foundations addition: color.status.neutral.{surface,surfaceStrong,content,contentStrong,border,icon} on the appearance axis, aliasing color.palette.neutral (light 100/600/800/0/300/600, dark 800/600/200/0/600/400), so that a category or a state without valence has a badge; four inventory contrast pairs added like the other statuses (content/surface 10.04 to 11.44, contentStrong/surfaceStrong 5.99, icon/surface 5.11 to 5.31, icon/surface.default 5.99 to 6.77; all 18 contexts pass). Brands inherit it through their palette.

Role names strongSurfaceColor and strongContentColor (suffix Color) because the role-type convention infers colors from surface, content, border or a Color suffix; the strong pair's contrast is guaranteed by the inventory pairs, not by the component report, which measures the subtle pair.
Leading icon at size.icon.xs (12 px) for every size: the indicator text is 11 to 14 px, so the 16 px icon of a sm Button would dominate; gap space.content.xs; optical placement like Button.
One line, truncated with an ellipsis when the width is short (table cells); the full label stays readable by assistive technology.
Strong appearance without a visible border (the strong surface already contrasts); the forced-colors edge is drawn in both appearances.

Box family of Counter: indicator typography (typography.indicator.{size}, 11/12/14 px), block size = line box, cap-height centering, minimum inline size = block size, radius.indicator, padding space.content.xs; a badge and a counter of the same size align. Sizes named like Button sizes, default md.

User decision at the contract gate (2026-10-16): Badge, Counter and Tag are distinct. Badge describes an object (status or category, read-only, set by the application); Counter says how many; Tag is a value the user manipulates (removable, sometimes selectable, often user-created). The trailing Counter and the dismissible option suggested at the first review belong to Tag: the trailing slot and space.content.2xs were withdrawn ("Ok ça me va"), and Tag is added to the catalog as a later candidate.
User decision at the contract gate (2026-10-16): neutral intent kept with the color.status.neutral.* roles (part of the accepted proposal).

User decision at the contract gate (2026-10-16): accent intent added ("pourquoi pas avoir l'intent accent pour le badge aussi"): new roles color.status.accent.* aliasing color.palette.accent and mirroring info (light 50/600/800/neutral.0/300/600, dark 950/600/200/neutral.0/800/400); four inventory contrast pairs. Listed after neutral since both are categories rather than statuses. Measured in the 18 contexts: content/surface 8.76 to 11.66, contentStrong/surfaceStrong 5.32 to 5.67, icon/surface 4.96 to 6.47, icon/surface.default 5.32 to 6.85.

User at the implementation review (2026-10-19): variant A, mixed case with the label clipped horizontally only; all caps rejected ("capitales ne fonctionne pas"). The comparison page examples/link-badge-review was removed once decided.

User at the Figma parity review (2026-10-20): the icon looked a little too far from the label. Cause: the glyph inset (1/8 of the icon) was compensated only before the icon, so the visible gap was leadingGap + 1.5 px. Now compensated on both sides as in Button: the drawing sits at leadingGap from the label (2, 4, 6 px by density); no token change.

User at the wave 1 Figma parity review (2026-10-26): "on expose la propriété Size des icônes dans les composants qui l'importent (genre badge) … la taille de l'icône ne devrait pas être modifiable dans ces composants mais décidée en amont et imposée dans le composant". The Figma master no longer nests the Icon component: the Phosphor glyph sits directly in the variants at the size the component imposes, behind an instance-swap property of the component; designers choose the glyph only. No code change (the code already imposes the size).
nextAction: None: Done within the declared scope (wave 1). Delivery (package publication, Figma library publication) is a separate approval; see authoring/roadmap.md.
implementationNotes: Markup: <span class="ggb-badge" data-intent data-appearance data-size> with the leading icon (aria-hidden) and <span class="ggb-badge__label">; no role (static text). Truncation with native text-overflow and the full label in a title-free visually hidden copy only if truncation hides it (decided at implementation).
No Bits UI primitive (static content), like Counter.
Implemented: block-size: 1lh so that the 12 px icon never grows the box; the strong appearance keeps a transparent inset edge; forced colors draw a 1 px CanvasText outline.

Implementation review (2026-10-17): descenders were cut in Safari (no overflow-clip-margin support); the label is now clipped horizontally only. All-caps alternatives shown for the reviewer's choice on examples/link-badge-review.
